title: [macOS Desktop] Capacity error silently stops overnight agent for 10 hours; manual Retry resumes

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Desktop app version `26.1021.31345`, build `21828` (installed as ChatGPT.app, bundle identifier com.openai.codex).
Local session metadata reports bundled CLI `0.164.0-alpha.11.1`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public report. The recorded error is `serverOverloaded`, not `usageLimitExceeded`; no claim is made about remaining account quota at the instant of failure.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS / Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm`.
Affected session metadata identifies `gpt-6.1-sol`.

### What issue are you seeing?

An agent left running overnight stopped on a model-capacity error roughly 13 minutes after its turn began. The user received no visible interruption alert and only discovered the stopped task the next morning. The next recorded turn started after manually clicking Retry, **10 hours 1 minute 4 seconds after the failure**.

The bug report concerns unattended recovery and failure notification, separately from the underlying capacity rejection. A user must not have to keep inspecting each conversation to discover that delegated overnight work has stopped.

Exact recorded error:

```json
{
  "message": "Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.",
  "codexErrorInfo": "serverOverloaded"
}
```

### Verified timeline

Times below are Asia/Taipei (UTC+08:00).

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-10-26 22:11:28 | Main turn starts. |
| 2026-10-26 22:23:58 | A subagent turn ends with the same capacity error. |
| 2026-10-26 22:24:45 | Main turn ends as failed with `serverOverloaded`, about 13m17s after it began. |
| 2026-10-27 08:25:49 | Next main-thread turn starts, with `turn_trigger: capacity_retry_manual`, after the user discovers the overnight stall and clicks Retry. |

A separate main conversation failed at 2026-10-27 16:49:21 and next started at 16:57:39, again with `capacity_retry_manual` (8m18s gap).

Within the inspected local project sessions from 2026-10-26 18:00 through 2026-10-27 approximately 17:05, there were four distinct terminal capacity failures: three main turns and one subagent turn. Forked transcript copies were deduplicated by turn ID. No `capacity_retry_automatic` task starts were found in that scope. Descendants can inherit a manual retry trigger, so these records are not being counted as separate user clicks.

These are task inactivity gaps, **not measurements of how long the backend remained overloaded**. Lower-level retries that do not create task starts are not ruled out.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start a substantial local development task in the desktop app, intended to continue unattended overnight.
2. Leave it running without babysitting the conversation.
3. A subsequent model request returns the capacity error above.
4. Return the next morning: the task has stopped; the user reports no failure notification.
5. Click Retry: a new model turn starts, as confirmed by the persisted manual retry trigger.

The capacity rejection is intermittent, so deterministic reproduction requires a capacity-error fixture or internal fault injection. No artificial extra model requests were used to reproduce it.

### Notification evidence and limits

- The user reports receiving no notification that the overnight job had stopped.
- Read-only inspection of local desktop logs found no corresponding `[desktop-notifications]` entry for any of the three failed main conversations within +/- 120 seconds of failure.
- This does not establish the macOS notification permission, Focus state, or app notification setting at those historical instants. Please investigate whether a terminal capacity failure generates an actionable failure notification at all, and whether delivery/suppression is observable.

### Expected behavior

- Persist and execute bounded capacity retries independently of whether the conversation is open or rendered; honor server retry delays and retain task state.
- Clearly distinguish running, retry scheduled, retry exhausted, and stopped awaiting user action.
- If the agent cannot continue automatically, issue a prominent, actionable interruption notification through the enabled notification channels. Do not silently leave an overnight task stopped until the user opens it.
- Show the time of the last attempt and whether another attempt is actually scheduled.
- Resume safely from the last checkpoint without duplicating completed tool side effects; preserve cancellation and approval boundaries. Do not silently change models without user consent.

### Additional information

Read-only inspection of this installed app found a feature-gated capacity-retry UI with a delay sequence `[10, 30, 120, 300]` and a `capacity_retry_automatic` path. Its existence does not establish that it was enabled or eligible for this account. No claim is made that UI mounting, feature gating, ownership, or retry exhaustion alone caused this occurrence; please correlate the relevant state internally.

User impact: the user intentionally delegated overnight work, then discovered in the morning that the agent had stopped shortly after starting and remained idle for about ten hours. The lack of an interruption alert made the lost working time invisible.

Related reports:
- #57128: similar overnight recovery gap in VS Code/WSL; this report supplies a macOS Desktop occurrence and notification evidence.
- #22390 and #32020: capacity retry and task continuity.

Private project contents, local paths, account identity, raw logs and conversation/turn IDs are intentionally omitted from this public issue. A sanitized local diagnostic record has been retained; correlation identifiers can be supplied through an official private support channel.
